contact.body:
Every product begins as an idea.

The difficult part isn't building it.
It's understanding what it wants to become.

Whether you're exploring a new venture, improving an existing product, or trying to make sense of a complex problem, I'd be happy to think it through with you.

Sometimes the outcome is a website.
Sometimes it's a prototype.

Sometimes it's realizing you don't need to build what you thought you needed.

Every conversation starts somewhere.

about.intro1: I run a lightweight product studio built to move from intention to working product without the overhead of a traditional team.
about.intro2: Strategy, design, engineering, AI, and deployment are usually treated as separate stages. I work across them as one continuous system, so decisions can stay connected from the first idea to the product in people's hands.

principles.title: Preserve the idea
principles.description: Every decision should reinforce the original problem instead of diluting it through disconnected handoffs.

principles.title: Build as one system
principles.description: Strategy, design, engineering, AI, and business decisions evolve together instead of being separated into isolated phases.

principles.title: Learn from reality
principles.description: Launching is not the end. Every product generates evidence that informs what comes next.

closing.line1: The projects below are connected by more than technology.
closing.line2: Whether the outcome becomes an AI platform, a blockchain protocol, or a physical product, the objective remains the same:
closing.line3: Reduce the distance between intention and understanding.

workWithMe.heroTitle: You don't need to assemble a product team for every product problem.
workWithMe.heroBody: I help early-stage product teams turn complex ideas into clear, working products — closing the gap between product thinking, system architecture, design and engineering, instead of hiring multiple specialists and hoping the handoffs hold.

problem.label: The Problem I Solve
problem.title: Most teams have the pieces. They're missing the connective tissue.
problem.body1: Strategy gets disconnected from design. Design gets disconnected from engineering. AI capabilities get bolted onto products without a coherent interaction model. Complex technical systems become hard to explain, use and ship. I work across the system, from definition through production, to close that gap.
problem.body2: The usual alternative is Founder → PM → designer → developer → QA → revisions. Every handoff adds interpretation, delay and rework. Working with me compresses that into one line: Founder or product team ↔ me.

problems: Product ambiguity — you know something should exist, not what it is yet.
Slow development caused by too much coordination between specialists.
Design and engineering handoffs that lose context every time work changes hands.
Getting stuck between a prototype and something you can actually ship.
Knowing what to build, but not having the person to carry it across the finish line.
Having an existing team, but needing extra product/design/engineering capacity for one initiative.

items.outcome: A functional product that can reach real users and generate real learning.

items.title: Accelerate the Product
items.subtitle: Your team doesn’t need another pair of hands. It needs momentum.

items.title: Keep the Product Moving

items.outcome: A product that keeps improving after launch, without staffing up to do it.

capabilities.label: What I Bring
capabilities.intro: Not five separate services. One connected skill set, applied to whichever situation above fits you.

engagement.body: These are typical starting points, not rigid packages — actual scope depends on the initiative. Each level is a different depth of commitment, not a separate, unrelated service.

process.label: My Process
process.title: One continuous cycle, not a handoff chain.

steps.description: Clarify the problem, the user, and the constraints before any solution takes shape.
Map the system — data, logic, and technical architecture — so complexity is visible early.
Shape the interface and experience around real usage, not assumptions.
Ship production-grade code, iterating in the open as the product takes form.
Release to real users with monitoring, security, and stability in place.
Study what the data and users reveal, then feed it back into the next cycle.

faqs.label: Frequently Asked Questions
faqs.title: Everything you need to know before we talk.

items.a: Yes. I'm based in Medellín and work remotely with clients internationally.
Yes — particularly founders and small product teams where product thinking and execution need to stay closely connected.

items.q: Can you join an existing team?
items.a: Yes. The role can be project-based or ongoing, depending on the product initiative.

items.q: Do you build the software yourself?
items.a: Yes. I handle product, design and engineering work directly rather than handing the project across a large production team.
Yes. AI-native tools and workflows are part of the studio's process, but AI doesn't replace product judgment, engineering decisions or human validation.

items.q: What if I only have an idea?
items.a: That’s a strong fit for the Discovery Sprint — figuring out what’s actually worth building comes first.

items.q: What if I already have a team?
items.a: I can join for a specific initiative where product, design and engineering need to move together.
Yes, but complex Web3 and protocol work is treated as a specialized engagement. For smart contracts, formal verification and security-sensitive systems, reach out directly.

A paid diagnostic, not a discounted Discovery Sprint. It answers what’s actually going on and what to prioritize next — useful on its own, and it can lead into a Discovery Sprint if a deeper product definition turns out to be needed.
